content.title: Paper Decision
content.metareview:_summary,_strengths_and_weakn:
This paper addresses the problem of overestimation in the multi-agent RL setting. It analyzes causes of overestimation and proposes an approach, DEMURE, which extends an existing approach, REDQ, to the multi-agent setting, and proposes additional regularization terms. The method is empirically evaluated in particle environment and starcraft tasks.

The reviewers agree that the paper addresses an important problem, and especially the analysis of the components that contribute to overestimation is found valuable.

At the same time, reviewers identify many open issues. The writing needs to be clearer, defining all key terms and concepts (e.g., c(s), hypernet). Pieces of writing and equations / proof parts taken from previous work need to be clearly marked as such (e.g., pieces taken from REDQ, theoretical results from previous work). The related work section is missing work that describes limitations of value based factorization for MARL. And a reviewer is concerned about the large number of hyperparameters introduced by this method.

The authors addressed some concerns in the rebuttal, but not all. In addition, the answer to questions about the number of hyperparameters raised additional concerns. The hyperparameter search method is involves a lot of conditional tuning to specifically control overestimation. This raises serious questions about the fairness of the empirical comparison, and about the generalizability of the results.

In sum, important concerns remain and we cannot recommend acceptance at this stage.
content.justification_for_why_not_higher_score: Serious questions about the approach and empirical evaluation remain. The paper is not ready for publication.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to solve the overestimation problem in the setting of multi-agent reinforcement learning. While there have been many works that tackled overestimation in single-agent setting, there haven’t been many works that aimed towards multi-agent RL overestimation problem. Previous works either extended ensemble methods in single-agent RL to multi agent overestimation, or softened max operator inn the bellman equations. This work aims to detailedly analyze the underlying causes, not only the overestimation of target q-values but also the accumulation of online Q-network during the optimization iterations. With this analysis, Dual Ensemble Multiagent Q-learning with hyper net Regularizer is proposed.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The strength of this paper comes from the section 3.1. Multiagent overestimation in estimation-optimization iterations, which analyzes that the term \partial Q_tot / \partial Q_i exacerbates the overestimation of target Q_tot thought he online Q_tot network optimizations. 
- Theorem 1 supports this claim. By applying the gradient method to minimize L_mix, Each Q_i is updated, and there is a \delta Q_i bias for Q_i. While in the case of Q_tot, the bias is 2 alpha N l^2 \delta y, showing that Q_i’s overestimation causes more severe overestimation for Q_tot during one optimization step, leading to the accumulation of bias. 
- Solution that this paper suggests is, regularize the \partial Q_tot / \partial Q_i term 
- Algorithm 1 Dual Ensemble Multiagent Q-learning is shown. The L1 regularization is used to restrict \pqrtial Q_tot / \pqrtial Q_i term. 
- Experiments are valid. 

Questions 

Q1. Although I’m convinced that restricting/ regularizing \partial Q_tot / \partial Q_i term to prevent the accumulation of overestimation errors, I’m not convinced by the existence of learnable term c(s), and the need for regularization the learnable term. Could you give me more explanation on the term c(s)? 

Q2. In Appendix E, the authors have suggested the hyper parameters of the DEMIX algorithm, H, N_H, K, N_K, and alpha_hyper. I think one weakness is that DEMIX algorithm has more hyper parameters to tune or search than S-QMIX and SM2-QMIX, WCU-QMIX. Is there a way to search the optimal range or set of hyper parameters? My guess is that the dimensionality grows rapidly since there are more hyper parameters to search than baseline methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This work is clear, well-written, and novel, but there are some questions that need to be addressed.
content.summary_of_the_review: I gave the score that is marginally below the threshold, but I am happy to raise the score during the discussion phase, if the questions are fully answered, and after discussion with other reviewers.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper extends an existing approach REDQ for dealing with Q value overestimation in (stochastic environment) single agent RL setting to value based multi agent RL (MARL). Experiments are provided on particle environment and Starcraft domains.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. The related works is incomplete. The paper lacks discussion about the representation limitations of using value based factorisation for MARL which is a major source of sub-optimality for these methods (refer to e.g. [1], [2]). This is important as the monotonic approximations tend to overestimate individual utilities and consequently joint action values even without noise in environment (See the simple matrix game in Maven [1] for e.g.). Discussion about the mentioned works should be included by the authors for better context and reader understanding.

2. The writing needs a lot of improvement. In general the paper is not very readable. Proofs should be moved to the appendix. The current notation used for describing the algorithms and equation is very dense and confusing, parts directly taken from the existing work REDQ should be highlighted. Same for the results taken from other works: Lemma 1, taken from Gan et al, should be clearly mentioned as such and the notation needs to be made consistent, Z has already been used for observation function, which makes it hard to follow the proof.

3. In general, the severe overestimation bias will be caused in joint Q only if l > 1, there are no such restriction in mixing networks of the value based methods (only l > 0). There should be some evidence provided to support if the former is the case.

4. Why is only a weak QMIX baseline used in experiments? There are more performant value based methods like [3] which should be used. Also why are win rates not reported for Starcraft, as is the standard? The noise added also doesn't seem significant compared to standard SMAC, how does it compare in scale?

References:
1. Maven: Multi-agent variational exploration, Mahajan et al, 2019
2. Tesseract: Tensorised Actors for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, Mahajan et al, 2021
3. Rode: Learning roles to decompose multi-agent tasks, Wang et al, 2021
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper needs lot of improvements for being readable (see above). 
The novelty is moderate only as the proposed method is taken from single agent RL. 
Important difficulties arising from representation constraints in MARL [1,2] are not discussed in the paper, which need to be added. The baselines are also not adequately strong.
The hyperparameter values are reported but the code is not, results relying on environment modifications may be difficult to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: The work needs lots of improvement before being ready for publication (see points above).

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper addresses overestimation issues in multi-agent RL, and shows that the issues not only come from target Q function for each individual agent, but also has an accumulated overestimation effect in the online global Q-network. To address his problem, the paper proposes Dual Ensembled MUltiagent Q-learning with hypernet REgularizer (DEMURE), that reduces the overestimation problem using random Q ensembles, and reduces accumulated overestimation using a hypernet regularizer. DEMURE is evaluated in multiagent particle (MPE) and noisy SMAC platform and is shown to outperform existing methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The paper identifies an important problem in multi-agent RL, and proposes a tentative solution. 
2. Experiments are relatively thorough. The proposed method is compared with multiple previous attempts to address the overestimation issues (e.g., soft Bellman/Mellowmax operator, TD3). 

Weakness
1. The theory part seems to be quite weak. In theorem 1, do you just assume all $\{Q_i\}$ have already been positively biased (and $\Delta Q_i \ge 2\alpha l \Delta y$)? If so then Theorem 1 seems to be trivial to me. Also, if our goal is to reduce $\partial Q_{tot} / \partial Q_i$, then how come it doesn't become $0$ (and thus we have a trivial $Q_{tot}$), if optimized properly? What are the counterforces that prevent it from happening? For now the reasoning is not clear. 

2. The writing quality is not great with many confusing parts. For example:

   a. What do you mean by "hypernet"? Do you mean a network that predicts the weights of other networks? How is hypernet related to $Q_{tot}$? It is supposed to reduce $\partial Q_{tot} / \partial Q_i$ but I didn't find the relationship between the hypernet (and its parameter $W$ and $B$) and $Q_{tot}$. To be honest, I am totally lost on how the regularization is enforced to reduce the overestimation issues, which unfortunately, is one of the key contributions of the work.  

   b. What is $c(s)$ in Eqn. 6? I cannot find its definition anywhere. In Sec. 3.3, it seems that $c$ is connected to hypernet. How is the two connected? 

3. In terms of experiments, what is the performance of DEMURE in noiseless SMAC? Will that hurt the performance?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. Clarity: The writing of the paper can be improved. 
2. Quality: the experiment sections seem to be ok, while the theory part seems to be quite weak. 
3. Novelty: the overestimation problem is important, but some part of the proposed solution is hard to understand (e.g., hypernet), so it is hard to evaluate the novelty properly. 
4. Reproducibility: the paper can be hard to reproduce, if the key contributions such as hypernet is not described clearly.
content.summary_of_the_review: Given the review, I think the paper can benefit more with substantial revision. So I vote for rejection.

content.title: Dual Ensembled Multiagent Q-Learning with Hypernet Regularizer
content.abstract: Overestimation in the temporal-difference single-agent reinforcement learning has been widely studied, where the variance in value estimation causes overestimation of the maximal target value due to Jensen's inequality. Instead, overestimation in multiagent settings has received little attention though it can be even more severe. One kind of pioneer work extends ensemble methods from single-agent deep reinforcement learning to address the multiagent overestimation by discarding the large target values among the ensemble. However, its ability is limited by the ensemble diversity. Another kind of work softens the maximum operator in the Bellman equation to avoid large target values, but also leads to sub-optimal value functions. Unlike previous works, in this paper, we address the multiagent overestimation by analyzing its underlying causes in an estimation-optimization iteration manner. We show that the overestimation in multiagent value-mixing Q-learning not only comes from the overestimation of target Q-values but also accumulates in the online Q-network's optimization step. Therefore, first, we integrate the random ensemble and in-target minimization into the estimation of target Q-values to derive a lower update target. Second, we propose a novel hypernet regularizer on the learnable terms of the online global Q-network to further reduce overestimation. Experiments on various kinds of tasks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently addresses the overestimation problem while previous works fail.
